clue.text: Pretty vacuous stuff, as in a pair of habits

indicators.note: vacuous means emptied, so the word pretty loses its inside letters and keeps only its two ends

parts.note: to stuff or cram is to jam
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sniffs that a nun's or monk's matching garments are rather empty stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habits' looks religious, but here it is just clothing. You wear pyjamas as a pair, and you wear them every night out of habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightwear comes as a set of top and trousers, and clothing can be called a habit, so the night suit is a pair of habits.

clue.text: Vessel takes a long time warming food

parts.note: a pot is a cooking vessel
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: A pot takes ages to heat up the dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a thick soup, a classic warming dish.

clue.text: Top steeplechaser, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a top is a knitted garment worn on the upper body, a sweater
a horse in a steeplechase leaps fences, so it is one that leaps

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a pullover sweater and anything that leaps, such as a horse running over fences.

clue.text: Author Thomas tours book fair in Parisian district

indicators.note: tours means goes around, so the author's name wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: Thomas More wrote Utopia
NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible
a mart is a market or fair

explanation.surface: A writer called Thomas visits a book fair held in part of Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Montmartre is the hilltop quarter of Paris known for artists and the Sacré-Cœur.

clue.text: Sloth, part Brazilian, sleeping upside down

indicators.note: in a down answer, upside down means the hidden letters are read from bottom to top
part says only some letters of the words that follow are used, taken across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A Brazilian sloth hangs upside down, asleep in the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' hides LIANS across 'Brazilian, sleeping'; 'upside down' turns it round. The sloth in the surface is the animal, but the definition means slowness, embodied by a slow creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth here is a slowcoach, and the garden mollusc is the proverbial slow mover.

clue.text: Turned over, grain soaks cooking vessel

indicators.note: turned over means the following pair of words is read backwards as one run

parts.note: the nap of fabric is its grain or pile
wets means soaks

explanation.surface: Grain is soaked and turned over in a pot, as in making porridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned over' reverses NAPWETS, the two pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a saucepan for stewing, a kind of cooking pot.

clue.text: Chicken partially boned?

definitions.meaning: having had only the backbone removed, so missing one bone

explanation.walkthrough: The chicken invites a kitchen reading, but it means a coward.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking courage is figuratively having no backbone, and a creature with its backbone taken out is literally so.

clue.text: Poet abandoning the top table

indicators.note: in a down answer the top is the first letter, which the poet's name loses

parts.note: John Keats was a Romantic poet

explanation.surface: A poet leaves the head of the dinner table.
explanation.definitionFit: A table can mean the food served, as in keeping a good table, and slang for food is this word.

clue.text: Constable, perhaps, catching breath, an individual collared

indicators.note: collared means seized and held round the neck, so one piece holds another

parts.note: panting is breathing hard to catch one's breath
I is one, a single individual

explanation.surface: A police constable, out of breath, collars a suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: Constable is not a police officer but John Constable, the English landscape artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture by the English landscape artist John Constable is an example of a work of art in oils.

clue.text: Observer simply reviewing Yankee Doodle: "Gutless"

indicators.note: re-viewing suggests looking over the letters again in a new order
gutless means with the insides removed, leaving the first and last letters of doodle

explanation.surface: A critic reviews the song Yankee Doodle and calls it gutless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewing' is the anagram signal, read as viewing again; 'Gutless' strips Doodle to its two ends before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: The unaided eye is the simple way to observe things, without telescope or microscope.

clue.text: Athenian money requiring flash investment

indicators.note: an investment puts something inside, as money is put into a venture

parts.note: tin is old slang for money
a mo is a moment, a flash

explanation.surface: Money from Athens needs a quick investment.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Timon of Athens is the play about the misanthropic citizen of that Greek city.

clue.text: Somewhat like 1 down? That's too much

definitions.meaning: 1 down is a soup, which is rather thick
an exclamation that something is unreasonable

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally describes a slightly thick soup, and idiomatically protests that something is unfair or excessive.

clue.text: Swimmer has old hair style

parts.note: grey hair suggests old age
a mullet is a haircut short at the front and long at the back

explanation.surface: A swimmer has an old-fashioned haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fish, so a creature that swims.

clue.text: Ladies' man — Agrippa, say?

definitions.meaning: a womaniser, a man with many female conquests
read as a gripper, a thing that grips, such as a press fastener

explanation.walkthrough: Agrippa was a Roman general, but read 'a gripper': a press fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a virile womaniser and also a press fastener that grips two pieces of cloth.

clue.text: Gear to change as went past

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone needed to change their gear as they went by.
explanation.definitionFit: Joggers' trousers are a kind of sports clothing, and gear means clothing.

clue.text: Maximum score on board, little time left in between, try to rebuild

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: rebuilding puts the pieces together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A darts player has little time left and must rebuild to reach the top score.
explanation.definitionFit: On a dartboard the narrow ring at the top segment scores sixty, the most a single dart can earn.

clue.text: Pathogen I guess consuming oxygen under blackhead

indicators.note: in a down answer, under means the following letters sit below the black piece

parts.note: read as black's head, the first letter of black

indicators.note: consuming means eating, so one piece takes another inside

parts.note: to hazard is to guess
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A spot on the skin could be an infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blackhead' splits into black's head, giving B.
explanation.definitionFit: A biological hazard is a danger from living organisms, such as a disease-causing germ.

clue.text: German statesman's doctrine dividing king and nipper after uprising

indicators.note: dividing means splitting another piece by going inside it
in a down answer, uprising means the pair of words is read bottom to top

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
a crab nips with its claws
an ism is a doctrine

explanation.surface: A German politician's doctrine divides the king from a little child.
explanation.walkthrough: A nipper looks like a child, but it is a shellfish. 'after uprising' turns the king and nipper into BARCK, which 'dividing' splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto von Bismarck was the Prussian chancellor who unified Germany; the 's stands for is.

clue.text: Very old figure breaking leg

indicators.note: breaking into means one piece is set inside another

parts.note: a stage is a leg of a journey
one is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: A statue breaks its leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The prehistoric period gives an adjective meaning extremely old-fashioned or ancient.

clue.text: Altercations getting out of hand between New York and California, perhaps

definitions.text: between New York and California, perhaps

indicators.note: out of hand means uncontrolled, so the letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Quarrels between people in New York and California get out of control.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes something running between two coasts, such as flights from the east coast to the west.

clue.text: Whine, seeing scorpion's tail in trousers being pulled up

indicators.note: in a down answer, pulled up means read from the bottom upwards
in places the tail letter inside the trousers

parts.note: Levi's are a brand of jeans

indicators.note: tail picks the last letter of scorpion

explanation.surface: Someone whines on finding a scorpion in their trousers as they pull them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts N inside LEVIS to make LEVINS, which 'being pulled up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: To whimper and complain tearfully is to whine.

clue.text: Stuff about English prince or king?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to gorge is to stuff oneself

explanation.surface: An English prince or king stuffs himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A common royal name, borne by several British kings and the young Prince of Wales's son.

clue.text: 24th chap detailed?

parts.note: a chap is a man
X is the 24th letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: The 24th man is described in detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' reads as de-tailed: without a tail, like the tailless cat breed from the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man's cat breed has no tail, so it is tailless, de-tailed.

clue.text: Cleaner cheek on bum

parts.note: to face someone out is to confront with cheek
to bum is to cadge or sponge

explanation.surface: Something for cleaning cheeks and bottoms.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft bathroom pad used for washing, so a cleaning tool.

clue.text: One or the other with a cold duck?

indicators.note: a blocked nose turns the th sound into a d, so the word is said as if bunged up

parts.note: either means one or the other

explanation.surface: Choose one or the other duck, and catch a cold.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a large sea duck prized for its down.

clue.text: See 25
Gather around to insist on a comfort break? Here's the bad news!

indicators.note: around means the gathering word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to reap is to gather a harvest
to demand is to insist on
a wee is a visit to the toilet

explanation.surface: A desperate person rounds people up to demand a toilet stop, and then delivers bad news.
explanation.definitionFit: A gloating poker player says this phrase on revealing a winning hand, news the losers won't like.

clue.text: Certainly not close to autumn, the night before last in summer

indicators.note: close means end, so the last letter of autumn

parts.note: eve is the evening before an event

indicators.note: last in picks the final letter of the word summer, its sixth

explanation.surface: Autumn's end, a holiday eve, and the last night of summer all blur together.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic refusal meaning not at any time, not on any account.

clue.text: Old man in want after potassium as protection for joint

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come behind the potassium symbol

parts.note: K is the chemical symbol for potassium

indicators.note: in places the father inside the word for want

parts.note: need is want
pa is father, one's old man

explanation.surface: An elderly man needs potassium to protect his joints.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded guard worn over the knee, which is a joint.

clue.text: Decide to do this puzzle again?

definitions.meaning: read as ..., solving the crossword once more

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to make up one's mind, and split with a hyphen it means solving a second time.
